_comment: Mechanical transcription of the 12 base-box Tag Team fighter boards.
Source: the PUBLIC BoardGameArena asset bundle (see sources.json) — no login needed.
Numbers and track layouts only. No card text, no art. tools/import_bga.py reads this.
hp_track is ordered BOTTOM (worst) to TOP (best), i.e. index 0 is the space a marker
can never be pushed below. Each entry is one space:
kind : 'hp' | 'ko' | 'revive' | 'spirit'
hp   : the printed number, when kind == 'hp' (absent when an icon replaces the number)
start: true on the space a marker is placed on at setup
icons: ops fired when the marker LANDS ON or PASSES THROUGH the space, except 'stop',
which halts movement immediately instead.
Op shape matches effects.py: {op, n, target}. target defaults to 'self'.

joan.name: Joan
joan.title: The Divine Shield
joan.profile: A Paladin who wins by never letting anyone down. Her Divine Voice feeds Power to the whole team a little at a time, and she attacks, blocks and heals well enough that she is rarely the wrong card to have drawn. The straightforward one, and none the weaker for it.
guide: Each Divine Voice gain moves the marker ONE space clockwise, and only the space it lands on pays. Two of the four pay; two do nothing.

_comment: Five printed positions, but a cycle of FOUR: the central Halo is where the marker
starts and it is never returned to. Clockwise Halo -> top_right -> bottom_right ->
bottom_left -> top_left -> top_right -> ... Ops fire on the LANDING space only.
MEASURED across the corpus, not read off the art. Joan's dial makes 21 first moves
and every one lands on 1; the transitions are 1->2 (39), 2->3 (34), 3->4 (31) and
4->1 (25), with not a single 4->0. Space 2 pays Joan 1 Power, space 4 pays her
Partner 1, and 1 and 3 pay nothing.
This file previously claimed the Halo IS re-entered, citing one table whose marker
'ran 0,1,2,4,2,4'. That reading was wrong. Wrapping onto the Halo makes the ring
five long where the real one is four, so from the second lap on Joan's Power came a
step LATE; the model before that had four outer spaces with the self-Power icon on
the first step out, which paid her a step EARLY. The log settles it in both
directions -- do not re-derive this from a picture of the board.

ching_shih.name: Ching Shih
ching_shih.title: The Pirate Queen
ching_shih.profile: She fights by building a Fleet. Ships do no damage on their own — they are options: much of her deck reads the number on the Fleet track and does something different above each threshold. Reach twenty and Terror of the Seas ends the Fight where it stands.
guide: Ships gained past 20 are ignored — the marker stops at the top of the Fleet track.
Reaching exactly 20 is what arms Terror of the Seas. At 16–19 it does nothing at all, so the last few Ships are worth holding a card for.

special_track._comment: Ships. Gains past 20 are ignored. No spaces carry ops; card text reads the value. The board rings 7, 10, 15 and 20 as thresholds cards refer to.

bodvar.name: Bödvar
bodvar.title: The Bearserker
bodvar.profile: All-out rage. Every card that feeds the Rage track drags him closer to turning over into the Berserker Bear, and almost nothing in the game hits as hard as what comes out the other side. The catch is the eleven health he has to stay standing on long enough to get there.
guide: His two-section cards read only the side matching the face-up board — the human half while he is Bödvar, the Bear half after.
On the Turn he transforms he ignores ALL health loss and healing, from every source. Tokens sitting on him come across to the Bear.
bodvar.note: The Bear arrives on as much health as Bödvar had Power at that instant, capped at 15 — a starting point, not a ceiling, so he can Heal above it later. He takes no health change at all on the turn he transforms, and his tokens come with him.

special_track._comment: Bottom space is the start. Each Rage gain steps up one. Reaching the top applies +3 Power and THEN flips the board to Berserker Bear.

back.name: Berserker Bear
back._comment: Initial HP = Bödvar's Power cubes at the moment of transformation, capped at 15; that is not a ceiling afterwards, the Bear may Heal to 15. Tokens carry over. He is immune to all HP change on the turn he transforms.

wong_fei_hung.name: Wong Fei-Hung
wong_fei_hung.title: The Old Master
wong_fei_hung.profile: He fights with your own strength. A Concentration token marks an opponent, and cashing it in Attacks them with THEIR Power rather than his; another card sets his Power to his Partner's, downwards as readily as up. And Crippling Touch removes a card from the game for good — the only thing in Tag Team that makes a deck smaller.
guide: He holds two Concentration tokens, so both opponents can be marked at once — and cashing one in takes it back from the Fighter it was cashed against.

the_wild_bunch.name: The Wild Bunch
the_wild_bunch.title: The Band of Outlaws
the_wild_bunch.profile: Five health and a Stop on every space, so nothing ever takes more than one off them — and nothing ever heals more than one back. The Fight is really about the Sheriff: several of their cards pay whoever is holding him, opponents included, so the token has to be in the right hands at the right moment.
guide: Every space on their Health track is a Stop, so the marker moves one space a Turn and no further. Hit and healed on the same Turn, they move ONE space in whichever direction is larger — not the difference.
The Sheriff pays whoever is holding him, opponents included, so passing him away at the wrong moment arms the other team.
the_wild_bunch._comment: Every HP space is worth one and the marker moves at most one space per turn, up or down, regardless of the total. That is encoded as a stop on every space below the top; the top is bounded by Max HP anyway.

shango.name: Shango
shango.title: The Keeper of Fire and Thunder
shango.profile: Fire that sticks. Every Aflame! token he places stays on its target for the rest of the Fight and makes his own Attacks hit harder, and a fifth on one Fighter is Incineration — an instant loss, however much health they had left. He starts on no Power at all, so the flames have to do the work, and getting them onto the right Fighter is the whole trick.
guide: Aflame! goes on the opposing ACTIVE Fighter. If they have none, every Aflame! on their Partner returns to Shango's supply first — the flames jump rather than spread.
Five Aflame! on one Fighter is Incineration and that team loses on the spot. It is not health loss, so nothing on a Health track can save them, and it beats a Double KO rather than drawing with it.
Flamepower is always on, including when his Partner is the one throwing his Attack.

maman_brijit.name: Maman Brijit
maman_brijit.title: The Immortal Sorceress
maman_brijit.profile: She turns a Fight around rather than winning it head-on: cancelling a card outright, stealing the healing meant for someone else, or bending the Attacks she caught onto the attacker's own Partner. And two KO spaces are not the end of her — pushed past both, she comes back on 4 health with a Power in hand.
guide: She has TWO KO spaces. On either at the end of a Turn she is KO'd; pushed past both onto the space below, she revives instead.
Once her marker is on the last space she loses no further health — unassigned loss does not carry over to the 4 health she comes back on.
maman_brijit._comment: Two KO spaces, and a revive space BELOW them. Pushed past both KOs onto the revive space she gains 1 Power and her marker returns to 4 at end of turn. The revive space is the bottom of the track, so further losses there are ignored.

mephisto.name: Mephisto
mephisto.title: The Agent of Darkness
mephisto.profile: Much of his deck asks which way the Serpent token is lying, and other cards turn it over — so the same card is two cards depending on when it comes up. Thirteen health and nothing much for his Partner, set against some of the nastiest single cards in the box, including one that turns any loss this Turn into a win.
guide: The Serpent token is flipped at random during setup, so which face he opens on is not yours to choose.
The Health-track icon flips the Serpent as the marker lands on OR passes through it, and neither face's effect applies at that moment — only the flip.
mephisto._comment: The Serpent token is double-sided and its setup face is random. The HP-track icon FLIPS it without applying the new face's effect.

mordred.name: Mordred
mordred.title: The Black Knight
mordred.profile: He would much rather you swung first. Mordred blocks, banks Power off the Bonus Action, and punishes the openings: Hidden Dagger only fires on a Turn nobody attacked, and Dark Power becomes an Attack the moment he reaches 8. Nineteen health to do it on, and no healing to speak of.
guide: No special track, no tokens, no setup. Everything he does is on his cards.

milady.name: Milady
milady.title: The Cloak and Dagger
milady.profile: She plants Schemes and lets them go off later. Eleven face-down tokens, drawn without replacement, running from a couple of Power to Poison, and three spaces on her own Health track unleash one when her marker reaches them. You cannot plan around what you cannot see — and neither can she.
guide: Her 11 Schemes are shuffled face down at setup. Plant one and it waits above her board; Unleash it and it is turned face up, applied, and removed from the Fight.

Schemes Unleashed from her HEALTH TRACK resolve after every card Action, in a mini-phase of their own — which is how they can move a marker that is sitting on a Stop. Poison always resolves last of all.
Run out of Schemes and a Plant does nothing.
milady._comment: Schemes unleashed from the HP TRACK resolve after all card actions, which is why they can move markers that are sitting on a stop. Schemes unleashed by a CARD resolve with that card.

golem.name: The Golem
golem.title: The Colossal Protector
golem.profile: A tank, with nothing pretending otherwise. Twenty-five health is the most in the game, three icons on the way down pay him Power for taking the hits, and his Presence can eat an Attack aimed at his Partner. Slow, obvious, and very hard to put down.
guide: The Presence stops ATTACKS only. Direct Damage, and anything else that costs health, goes straight through it.
Reanimation makes the next card resolve twice, and the second pass reads the state the first one left — so a token assigned on the first pass is already there for the second.
_comment: Protect the Innocent invests: the Golem takes 3 and his Partner gains his
presence. The token is a ONE-SHOT SHIELD -- the next Attack aimed at whoever
holds it is negated and the token comes back to the Golem, which is what lets
the card be played for its investment again later. Read straight off BGA's log:
902218046 f1t2 'The Wild Bunch attacks Bodvar' -> Bodvar loses no health ->
'The Golem gains [token]', and 886355216 f2t2 where Maman Brijit DEFLECTS the
Golem's own Attack onto his partner Milady and the presence eats it.
Modelling it as a permanent flag stuck the card's if/else on 'partner has it'
after one play, so the Golem never paid the 3 again.

the_fey_folk.name: The Fey Folk
the_fey_folk.title: The People of the Forest
the_fey_folk.profile: Three Characters — Fairy, Gnome and Elf — but only one is ever on the board, and only that one can be hurt or healed. Lose the last of a Character's health and they become a Spirit; you then choose who steps in, at full health. The Spirit track counts them and starts at 1 before anyone has fallen, so their cards are already paying from the first Turn. No Character has a KO space: the only way the Fey Folk lose is All Legends Must Pass being revealed while all three are Spirits.
guide: Only the Character on the board can lose health or be Healed. The other two are waiting, untouchable, at full health.
The Spirit track starts at 1 before anyone has fallen, so a card that pays 'per Spirit' is already paying on Turn 1. Each Character that falls adds one.
A Character becomes a Spirit at the END of the Turn: the Spirit track goes up, then you choose who comes in, then their Start space icon fires. That icon can fire many times over a Fight.
With all three gone they still play their cards — they simply cannot lose or recover health. Cards count the Spirits as they stood at the START of the Turn.
_comment: Three Characters share one fighter slot. Only the ACTIVE character has a marker on a
track and can lose or recover HP. A character's tracks have no KO: losing the last HP
moves the marker to the Spirit space instead. At the END of that turn, before the next
card, the Spirits track advances one and the player picks the next active character,
placing its marker on the TOP space of its track and applying that space's icons.
They start the game with 1 Spirit already counted. They are KO only if all three are
Spirits at the START of the turn 'Toutes les legendes ont une fin' is revealed.
